title: Compilation + Unit-Test Prompt Bank: Inspection Notes & Regression Heuristics
body:
Purpose:
This is a working inspection notebook for the new compilation + unit-test prompt bank we plan to onboard as part of model acceptance gating. The focus is on realistic engineer-facing prompts that stress: 1) code that must compile in common toolchains (python3.10, go1.20, javac 17), 2) generation of minimal unit tests that can be executed in CI, and 3) adherence to simple style constraints (type hints, linter-compatible formatting, no global side effects).

Scope and motivation:
- We need prompt templates that produce code+tests reliably so our regression harness can run end-to-end: synthesize code -> run static checks -> run unit tests -> surface diffs.
- The bank is intentionally small (80–120 prompts) but diversified by language, problem class, and refactor surface area (API rename, extract method, optimize loop).

Structure of each prompt in the bank (informal):
- Short title line (one sentence)
- Natural language spec (2–4 sentences; includes input/output examples)
- Constraints: compile command, test framework, style bullets (e.g., use type hints, avoid global state)
- Golden inputs: 2–3 unit test cases to include in generation
- Scoring rubric: compile_ok boolean, tests_passed_count, lint_warnings_count, semantic_similarity_score (tool)

Representative prompt examples (sketches):
1) Python: "Implement function merge_sorted_iterators(a, b) that yields sorted items from two sorted iterators. Must be memory-efficient (no materialization). Include pytest unit tests for edge cases: empty iterators, repeated values, infinite generator truncated by islice." Constraints: python3.10, run: pytest -q, style: type hints required.

2) Go: "Implement a small package 'interval' with an 'Intersect' function that returns overlapping intervals. Provide table-driven tests using the testing package and a benchmark stub." Constraints: go1.20, go vet and go test; no global vars.

Evaluation/CI integration notes:
- Local harness command (developer): ./scripts/run_prompt_eval.sh --model $MODEL --prompt-bank path/to/bank.json --out results/$MODEL.json --max-requests 200
- CI job (PR gating): 1) run static/compile; 2) run tests with timeout 30s per test-suite; 3) collect artifacts: compiled binary/logs, pytest xml, linter output.
- Failure categories to bubble up in dashboard: COMPILE_FAIL, RUNTIME_ERROR, TEST_FAILURE, STYLE_VIOLATION, FLAKY_TEST (non-deterministic).

Metrics and thresholds (initial proposals):
- Compile rate >= 92% on non-trivial prompts (i.e., excluding toy one-liners).
- Deterministic test pass rate >= 85% (averaged across seeds).
- Lint warnings per prompt <= 2 for python prompts.
- Regression tolerance: if a new model drops compile_rate by >4% or test_pass_rate by >6% vs baseline, block rollout and trigger triage.

Grading heuristics (quick):
- compile_ok: run language-specific compile/run command inside container; if exit_code != 0 -> COMPILE_FAIL.
- tests_passed_count: parse test runner output. For pytest use junit xml parsing.
- style_score: map linter warnings to penalty points; >5 penalty -> STYLE_VIOLATION.
- flakiness: re-run failing tests with different random seeds; if non-deterministic, flag FLK and log seeds.

Failure mode examples and notes for triage:
- Missing imports vs. wrong API surface: often model uses third-party API name incorrectly. Triage: add targeted prompts that include import lines and example API usage.
- Overly verbose test scaffolding: models sometimes produce long integration-style tests; prefer focused unit tests. Add constraint line: "Test only the function you implement; do not use external network calls."
- Stateful singletons: model sometimes emits module-level state. Add constraint: "No process-global mutable state; use local variables or class instances."

Quick TODOs / next steps:
- (Dev) Expand bank with 12 more Python prompts covering async functions and type generics. Owner: Samira. Due: 2026-03-15.
- (QA) Add mutation-based checks to detect brittle tests. Owner: Devon. Due: 2026-03-22.
- (Infra) Add new CI step to collect pytest junit xml and attach to model eval runs. Owner: Elena. Due: 2026-03-10.

Open questions / discussion points:
- Should we accept generated mocks/stubs as long as they are isolated and non-networking? Tradeoff between realism and flakiness.
- What is an acceptable linter baseline: black/flake8 vs. pylint? Proposal: black + flake8 for now.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep prompt wording minimal but explicit about compile command and test command.
- Record model seed used for reproducibility.
- We probably need a separate small bank targeting code-refactors that preserve API but change internals; that will be a follow-up doc.

Attaching this as a working doc — please add comments inline for any prompt that regularly results in COMPILE_FAIL so we can iterate on constraints and golden examples.
